newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bondholders want new directors.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bondholders want new directors.

text.p: The Official Committee of Bondholders of Marvel Holdings, Inc., Marvel Holdings Inc and Marvel III Holdings Inc said Friday it told the Marvel Entertainment Group Inc that it intends to vote a majority of Marvel Entertainment equity to elect a new board of directors on March 25.

Carl Icahn and six other candidates are on the bondholders slate. Two more directors would be selected by the shareholders. The bondholders said their due diligence reveals Marvel is in complete disarray and immediate action is needed to save the company.

The bondholders added they will continue to guarantee a $365 million capital infusion pursuant to a rights offering, subject to the replacement of the Marvel board and confirmation by the bankruptcy court of an acceptable reorganization plan. The bondholders said they intend to use the $365 million to recapitalize Marvel and to restore the company to financial and operational health.

In a letter sent to Marvel on Friday by counsel to the bondholders, they said the decision to replace the board "is driven by the critical and interrelated needs to halt Marvel's deterioration and to promote Marvel's proper reorganization."

The bondholders also charged that Marvel refuses to try to undo the damage of its disastrous licensing program which sacrificed Marvel's long-term growth and opportunity so as to inflate artificially Marvel's earnings per share.

They cited one of Marvel's former officers as telling some members of the committee that his orders were "to get earnings at any cost." Another officer, said the bondholders, unabashedly told these same members that the entire premise of the formation of Toy Biz was the creation of immediate earnings, not greater liquidity, cash flow or future growth.

Marvel, charged the bondholders, "clearly has no truly rehabilitative plan of reorganization "and already has suffered the damage of six months spent recklessly promoting the interests of the Andrews Group and unadvisedly seeking to enrich the Toy Biz inside shareholders."
Representatives from Marvel could not immediately be reached.
